items.stem: What problem does RAII solve in C++?

options.text: It ties a resource's lifetime to an object's scope so cleanup happens automatically, even on exceptions
options.rationale: Correct: RAII acquires in the constructor and releases in the destructor, guaranteeing cleanup when the object goes out of scope.

options.text: It makes all allocation happen on the stack
options.rationale: RAII manages lifetime; the resource can still live on the heap.
RAII works with exceptions; it does not disable them.

options.text: It forces manual delete calls everywhere
options.rationale: RAII removes the need for manual delete, the opposite of this.

items.explanation: Correct: RAII acquires in the constructor and releases in the destructor, guaranteeing cleanup when the object goes out of scope.

items.stem: Which statements about unique_ptr and shared_ptr are correct? (Select TWO)

options.text: unique_ptr expresses exclusive ownership and cannot be copied
options.rationale: Correct: unique_ptr is move-only and models a single owner.

options.text: shared_ptr uses reference counting and can create cycles that leak
options.rationale: Correct: cyclic shared_ptrs keep each other alive; weak_ptr breaks the cycle.

options.text: shared_ptr is always faster than unique_ptr
options.rationale: shared_ptr carries reference-counting overhead unique_ptr does not.

options.text: unique_ptr requires manual delete to free its resource
options.rationale: unique_ptr frees automatically in its destructor.

items.explanation: Correct: unique_ptr is move-only and models a single owner.; Correct: cyclic shared_ptrs keep each other alive; weak_ptr breaks the cycle.

items.stem: You modify a std::vector by inserting elements while holding an iterator into it. What is the risk?

options.text: Insertion can reallocate the buffer, invalidating existing iterators
options.rationale: Correct: growth may move the storage, so previously obtained iterators dangle.
Vectors do not become read-only; the issue is iterator invalidation.

options.text: Nothing; vector iterators are always stable
options.rationale: Vector iterators are not stable across reallocation.
Insertion does not sort the vector.

items.explanation: Correct: growth may move the storage, so previously obtained iterators dangle.
